Palantir Technologies Inc. (PLTR) reported $2.31 billion in revenue for the quarter ended September 2026, representing a year-over-year increase of 95.9%. EPS of $0.44 for the same period compares to $0.21 a year ago.

The reported revenue compares to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.17 billion, representing a surprise of +6.54%. The company delivered an EPS surprise of +7.32%, with the consensus EPS estimate being $0.41.

While investors scrutinize revenue and earnings changes year-over-year and how they compare with Wall Street expectations to determine their next move, some key metrics always offer a more accurate picture of a company's financial health.

Since these metrics play a crucial role in driving the top- and bottom-line numbers, comparing them with the year-ago numbers and what analysts estimated about them helps investors better project a stock's price performance.

Here is how Palantir Technologies performed in the just reported quarter in terms of the metrics most widely monitored and projected by Wall Street analysts:

Customers: 1,090 versus the four-analyst average estimate of 1,114.

Geographic Revenue- United States - Government: $953 million versus the seven-analyst average estimate of $874.3 million.

Geographic Revenue- United States - Commercial: $984 million versus the seven-analyst average estimate of $913.91 million.

Revenue- Government: $1.15 billion versus the eight-analyst average estimate of $1.04 billion. The reported number represents a year-over-year change of +81.8%.

Revenue- Commercial: $1.17 billion versus $1.13 billion estimated by eight analysts on average. Compared to the year-ago quarter, this number represents a +113.3% change.

Palantir Technologies (PLTR) Q3 2026 highlights:

Revenue $2.31 billion vs S&P analysts' consensus estimates of $2.18 billion (95.9% year-on-year growth, 5.9% beat)

Adjusted EPS $0.44 vs S&P analysts' consensus estimates of $0.41 (8.1% beat)

Revenue growth

A company's long-term revenue performance can indicate its overall quality. Any business can deliver a good quarter or two, but many enduring ones grow for years. Palantir Technologies's revenue grew at a strong 38.5% compounded annual growth rate over the last five years. Its growth surpassed the average software company and shows its offerings resonate with customers.

Palantir Technologies quarterly revenue

Long-term growth matters most, but within software, a half-decade historical view may miss recent innovations or disruptive industry trends. Palantir Technologies's annualized revenue growth of 66% over the last two years is above its five-year trend, suggesting demand was strong and recently accelerated.

Palantir Technologies year-on-year revenue growth

This quarter, Palantir Technologies reported year-on-year revenue growth of 95.9%, and its $2.31 billion of revenue beat Wall Street's consensus estimates by 5.9%. Management is currently guiding for an 88.4% year-on-year increase in revenue next quarter.

Looking further ahead, sell-side analysts expect revenue to grow 54.8% over the next 12 months, according to S&P, a deceleration versus the last two years. Despite the slowdown, this projection is strong and implies the market is pricing in success for its products and services.

The customer acquisition cost (CAC) payback period measures the months a company needs to recoup the money spent on acquiring a new customer. This metric helps assess how quickly a business can break even on its sales and marketing investments.

title: Palantir Grows Revenue 96% as New Deals Slow: Rapid Earnings Reaction
detail:
Palantir Grows Revenue 96% as New Deals Slow: Rapid Earnings Reaction
David Kretzmann, The Motley Fool
Mon, November 2, 2026 at 2:44 PM MST 3 min read
PLTR
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) grew third-quarter revenue 96% to about $2.31 billion and raised its full-year outlook again. Shares were up about 2% in after-hours trading. The business is turning growth into profit at a rare pace. But new contract signings barely grew, so future growth depends on signings picking up.

Key numbers

Revenue: $2.31 billion, up 96% from $1.18 billion a year ago.

U.S. commercial revenue: $984 million, up 148% from a year ago.

GAAP operating margin: 47%, up from 33% a year ago.

Full-year revenue guidance: Raised to about $8.53 billion, or 91% growth.

What it means

U.S. commercial revenue passed U.S. government revenue for the first time, with government at $953 million. Government contracts are big and sticky, but budgets move slowly. Commercial customers can expand fast once one deployment pays off. That speeds growth but adds exposure to corporate spending cycles.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Profit outran sales because most of Palantir's costs don't rise with revenue. Operating expenses grew about 46% while revenue nearly doubled. Software costs little to deliver once it's built, so most of each new dollar falls to profit.

The soft spot is new business. Palantir closed $2.92 billion in total contract value, up just 6% from a year ago. Revenue is recognized from contracts already signed. When signings grow far slower than sales, the company works through its backlog faster than it refills it. Big deals are lumpy, so one soft quarter isn't a trend yet.

What to watch next

The key number is U.S. commercial remaining deal value, which rose just 4% from last quarter while U.S. commercial revenue rose 29%. If that backlog doesn't speed up, today's growth rate will be hard to hold.

Palantir Technologies Inc. (PLTR) came out with quarterly earnings of $0.44 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.41 per share. This compares to earnings of $0.21 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +7.32%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this company would post earnings of $0.35 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.41, delivering a surprise of +17.14%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

Palantir Technologies, which belongs to the Zacks Internet - Software industry, posted revenues of $2.31 billion for the quarter ended September 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 6.54%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $1.18 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

Palantir Technologies shares have added about 3.6% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 10.7%.

What's Next for Palantir Technologies?

While Palantir Technologies has underperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for Palantir Technologies was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $0.46 on $2.45 billion in revenues for the coming quarter and $1.62 on $8.21 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.
